name: THC
reported_effects: Community-reported: euphoria, altered sensory perception, relaxation, appetite stimulation. Intoxicating. Effects vary by dose, route, and individual.
notes: Primary intoxicating cannabinoid in most drug-type chemovars. Vapor temp commonly cited ~157 C; actual volatilization depends on device and flower moisture.

name: THCA
reported_effects: Community-reported: non-intoxicating in raw acid form. Converts to THC on heating/decarboxylation.
notes: Dominant cannabinoid in raw/unheated flower. Decarboxylates to THC roughly in the 105-120 C range over time. No single published vapor temp - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: THCV
reported_effects: Community-reported: at low doses, clear-headed and stimulating; at higher doses, THC-like intoxication. Shorter-acting per user reports.
notes: Propyl analogue of THC. Vapor temp commonly cited ~220 C; verify against lab source.

name: CBD
reported_effects: Community-reported: calming, relaxing, non-intoxicating. Frequently discussed alongside THC for balanced experiences.
notes: Major non-intoxicating cannabinoid in fiber-type and many hybrid chemovars. Vapor temp commonly cited ~180 C.

name: CBDA
reported_effects: Community-reported: non-intoxicating raw acid precursor of CBD.
notes: Decarboxylates to CBD on heating. No published single vapor temp - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: CBN
reported_effects: Community-reported: sedating, sleepy qualities; often associated with aged or oxidized flower. Mildly intoxicating.
notes: Oxidation/degradation product of THC - concentrations rise as flower ages. Vapor temp commonly cited ~185 C.

name: CBG
reported_effects: Community-reported: mild, clear-headed, non-intoxicating at common doses.
notes: Biosynthetic precursor ('mother cannabinoid') to THC/CBD/CBC. Vapor temp values in circulation conflict (104-220 C cited) - no reliable single published value; flagged for lab sourcing.

name: CBGA
notes: Parent acid from which THCA/CBDA/CBCA branch. Vapor temp not reliably published - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: CBC
reported_effects: Community-reported: mood-elevating qualities; often discussed as part of the 'ensemble' with THC. Non-intoxicating at common doses.
notes: Usually minor in modern chemovars. Vapor temp not reliably published - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: CBL
reported_effects: Community-reported: effects largely undocumented - honesty note: pharmacology essentially unstudied.
notes: Minor degradation product related to CBC. Very thin literature; vapor temp unknown.

name: delta-8-THC
reported_effects: Community-reported: THC-like but commonly described as milder and clearer. Intoxicating.
notes: Structural isomer of delta-9-THC, typically converted from CBD. Vapor temp commonly cited ~175 C; thinner evidence base than delta-9.

name: delta-10-THC
reported_effects: Community-reported: energizing, 'sativa-like' character - thin evidence; consumer products rarely independently verified.
notes: Trace naturally; usually synthesized. No reliable published vapor temp.

name: THCP
reported_effects: Community-reported: extremely potent THC-like effects. Laboratory binding studies (2019) suggest high CB1 affinity - no human clinical data.
notes: Identified in 2019 (Italian research team). Alkyl side-chain heptyl analogue. Vapor temp not published.

name: CBDP
reported_effects: Community-reported: effects essentially undocumented - included for completeness.
notes: CBD heptyl homologue, identified alongside THCP in 2019. Under active study; vapor temp not published.

name: Myrcene
aroma: musky, earthy, herbal; ripe mango, hops
notes: Most prevalent terpene across modern chemovars per community/lab surveys. Boiling point well established in chemistry literature (~167 C).

name: Limonene
notes: Very common in citrus-forward and dessert-lineage strains. Literature boiling point ~176 C.

name: alpha-Pinene
notes: Among the most abundant terpenes in nature; literature boiling point ~155 C.

name: beta-Pinene
notes: Often co-occurs with alpha-pinene. Literature boiling point ~166 C.

name: beta-Caryophyllene
notes: Cannabis charts commonly cite ~130 C vapor temp; atmospheric boiling point differs (vacuum bp 129 C at 15 mmHg) - flagged for lab sourcing. Sesquiterpene.

name: alpha-Humulene
notes: Common in hops; literature boiling point commonly cited ~198 C. Sesquiterpene.

name: Linalool
notes: Literature boiling point ~198 C. Found across floral-aroma strains.

name: Terpinolene
aroma: floral, herbal, piney with citrus lift
notes: Signature of many classic sativas (Haze family etc. per community reports). Literature boiling point ~186 C.

name: beta-Ocimene
notes: Literature boiling point for trans-beta-ocimene commonly cited ~177 C; verify isomer against lab source.

name: Nerolidol
notes: Sesquiterpene alcohol. Boiling point commonly quoted is vacuum (122 C at 12 mmHg); no reliable single atmospheric vapor temp - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: alpha-Bisabolol
notes: Cannabis literature commonly cites ~160 C vapor temp; atmospheric bp not established in a single source - flagged for lab sourcing.

name: Geraniol
notes: Literature boiling point ~230 C. Common in dessert-lineage strains.

name: Camphene
notes: Literature boiling point ~159 C. Often minor component.

name: delta-3-Carene
notes: Literature boiling point ~168-171 C. Often minor component.

name: Cannaflavin A
notes: Prenylated flavone first described in cannabis (1980s); being studied for inflammatory pathways in preclinical models. Vapor temp not published.

name: Cannaflavin B
notes: Prenylated flavone; formula pending verification against primary literature - flagged.

name: Cannaflavin C
notes: Most recently described cannaflavin; thin literature. Formula pending verification - flagged.

name: Quercetin
notes: Widespread plant flavonoid also present in cannabis. Vapor temp not published for cannabis context.

name: Kaempferol
notes: Widespread plant flavonoid also present in cannabis. Vapor temp not published for cannabis context.

name: Cannabisativine
notes: HONESTY NOTE: cannabinoids/terpenes dominate cannabis phytochemistry; alkaloids occur only in trace amounts and are severely understudied. Reported from cannabis roots/leaves in older literature.

name: Anhydrocannabisativine
notes: HONESTY NOTE: minor class - trace occurrence, very thin literature, no published vapor temp or established role.
